edges.mechanism: Co-component of the AREDS/AREDS2 formula (zinc 80 mg or 25 mg + copper 2 mg with L/Z 10/2 mg); zinc alone slowed AMD progression. Lowering zinc from 80 to 25 mg did not change progression at 5 or 10 years. AREDS zinc linked to genitourinary problems in men; no high- vs low-dose difference in AREDS2.
edges.evidence: AREDS RCT, AREDS2 secondary randomization and 10-y follow-up (HR low vs high zinc 1.04, 0.94-1.14), Cochrane 2023; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Vitamin C 500 mg is a fixed co-component of the AREDS2 formula in which L/Z replaced beta-carotene; benefit is established for the combined formula, not for individual components.
edges.evidence: AREDS/AREDS2 RCTs and Cochrane review; moderate certainty for the combination

edges.mechanism: Vitamin E 400 IU is a co-component of the AREDS2 formula; alone it did not prevent AMD (RR 0.97) and may slightly raise late AMD risk.
edges.evidence: AREDS2 design; Cochrane prevention review (4 RCTs, n=55,614); moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Tested factorially with L/Z in AREDS2: no interaction and no added benefit for AMD progression or cognition; no evidence of harm from co-use.
edges.evidence: AREDS2 RCT (n=4203) and cognitive substudy (n=3501); high certainty for absence of added benefit

edges.mechanism: Xanthophylls share micellar/SR-BI absorption routes; high-dose single xanthophylls lowered other xanthophylls in non-retinal tissues in chicks. In humans, 6 mg astaxanthin + 10 mg L + 2 mg Z still raised MPOD over 8 weeks.
edges.evidence: One human RCT of the combination plus animal/mechanistic data; very low certainty of a clinically relevant interaction

edges.mechanism: Lutein and lycopene compete for incorporation into chylomicrons postprandially, but 3-week co-supplementation did not lower plasma status; lycopene did not reduce lutein uptake in Caco-2 cells.
edges.evidence: Human postprandial and 3-week crossover data plus in vitro; low certainty, probably not clinically important

edges.mechanism: Beta-carotene competes with lutein for intestinal uptake (about 20% lower in Caco-2) and lowered retinal L/Z at high intake in chicks; in AREDS2 it was associated with more lung cancer (OR 1.82 at 10 y) mostly in former smokers, while L/Z outperformed it for late AMD (HR 0.82; 10-y HR 0.85).
edges.evidence: AREDS2 RCT and 10-y follow-up, ATBC/CARET, mechanistic data; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Lipase inhibition reduces absorption of fat-soluble carotenoids (beta-carotene dose absorption about one-third lower; plasma alpha/beta-carotene down 45%/32% over 4.5 months, L/Z unchanged in n=6). Label advises a multivitamin taken at least 2 h before or after orlistat.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (n=48), small cohort (n=6), FDA label; low certainty for L/Z specifically

edges.mechanism: Cholestyramine/colestipol/colesevelam bind bile acids needed for micellar absorption of fat-soluble nutrients (cholestyramine cut vitamin A absorption 59.5%); labels advise separating doses (1 h before or 4-6 h after cholestyramine; vitamins at least 4 h before colesevelam).
edges.evidence: Human absorption study for vitamin A plus drug labels; no direct L/Z data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lutein uptake is partly NPC1L1-mediated; ezetimibe inhibited up to 40% of lutein accumulation in Caco-2 cells.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; no human data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: L/Z are transported mainly on HDL/lipoproteins; atorvastatin (not rosuvastatin) lowered MPOD in a small study and MPOD fell with longer statin duration. 44% of AREDS2 participants used statins.
edges.evidence: Cross-sectional and small case-series data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Phytosterols reduce micellar carotenoid absorption: 6.6 g/d lowered plasma lutein 14%; 18-month stanol/sterol margarine lowered serum L/Z without lowering MPOD.
edges.evidence: Controlled human trials; low certainty for clinical relevance

edges.mechanism: Lutein esters need more dietary fat than carotenes for absorption: plasma lutein rose 207% with 36 g fat vs 88% with 3 g fat; oil-based/self-emulsifying formulations raise bioavailability.
edges.evidence: Human RCT and PK studies; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Beta-carotene formulas raise lung cancer in smokers/former smokers, so L/Z (AREDS2) formula is preferred; L/Z itself showed no significant lung-cancer excess in AREDS2 (OR 1.15, 0.79-1.66), but long-term individual lutein supplement use was associated with lung cancer in the VITAL cohort (HR 2.02).
edges.evidence: RCTs (AREDS2, ATBC, CARET) and one observational cohort; low certainty for lutein itself

edges.mechanism: Indication: AREDS antioxidant+zinc formula slows progression (OR 0.72); L/Z is the preferred carotenoid in that formula (vs beta-carotene HR 0.82) and slowed GA growth toward the fovea; L/Z alone has little effect (RR 0.94).
edges.evidence: AREDS, AREDS2, Cochrane 2023; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Adipose tissue competes with retina for L/Z; MPOD inversely related to BMI/body fat (about 21% lower MP in BMI >29), and waist circumference/diabetes predict lower MPOD.
edges.evidence: Cross-sectional studies; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Hypothyroidism and diabetes predispose to hypercarotenaemia/carotenodermia at ordinary carotenoid intakes; adding high-dose lutein makes skin yellowing more likely.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: L/Z 10/2 mg in pregnancy raised maternal macular pigment and 5-fold cord-blood L/Z without reported harm; 6-12 mg/d in lactation raised breast-milk lutein 140-250% and infant plasma lutein.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs (L-ZIP; lactation RCT n=89); low certainty

edges.mechanism: High lutein intake causes carotenodermia (yellow skin, palms/soles) that can be mistaken for jaundice; it reflects carotenaemia, not hyperbilirubinaemia.
edges.evidence: Case report, supplementation study and review; low certainty

edges.with: skin carotenoid score (resonance Raman / reflection spectroscopy)
edges.mechanism: Supplemental L/Z raises skin carotenoid readings used as an objective fruit/vegetable-intake biomarker, overstating dietary intake.
edges.evidence: RCTs showing skin carotenoid increases with L/Z (L-ZIP, central obesity RCT) and biomarker validation review; moderate certainty

edges.with: macular pigment optical density vs serum carotenoids
edges.mechanism: In AREDS2 participants MPOD did not correlate with serum or skin carotenoids, so serum L/Z is a poor proxy for retinal status; MPOD response is largest with low baseline.
edges.evidence: AREDS2 ancillary imaging study and MA; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Variants in carotenoid transport/lipid genes (SCARB1 rs11057841, RPE65 rs4926339, ABCA1 rs1929841, FADS1 rs174534) were associated with MPOD response to supplementation.
edges.evidence: Candidate-gene study in TwinsUK (n=310), unreplicated; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: CFH and ARMS2 risk alleles did not modify response to L/Z vs beta-carotene, low vs high zinc, or omega-3 in AREDS2; genotype-guided formula selection is not supported.
edges.evidence: AREDS2 genetic analysis (1684 participants); moderate certainty for no interaction
